_doc: Disposition store for the open-question register (DIRECTOR_RULING_NO_QUESTION_LEFT_UNANSWERED 2026-07-28, deliverables 1+2). The QUESTION SET is NOT stored here -- it is DERIVED from primary state (the ruling bodies) by background/open_question_register.py, so it can never silently omit a real question. This file holds ONLY the human judgement: for each question_key, its disposition. A question with NO entry here is 'open' (silent) and BLOCKS archival of its ruling. Statuses: answered|unknown|not_measurable|wrong CLOSE a question (unblock archival); 'carried' is NON-SILENT (has a reason) but UNANSWERED, so it still blocks. Keys are stable 12-char ids (see question_key()).

58f8fa8364c2.question: Stall-set coverage verdict on the four events (console rescue, publish-gate wedge >1h, origin freeze >30m, advisor restart-ruling): detected / detector-added / argued-out?
58f8fa8364c2.disposition: ANSWERED (2026-07-28, per-event, evidence-cited): coverage is PARTIAL. (1) Console rescue -- NOT detected as an event; only its symptom is caught (deadmans_switch.py commit-cadence BLOCKED/STALL tiers fire when no meaningful commit lands within the window). The counter-reset it should trigger depends on the unbuilt exit-criterion counter (see Q2). (2) Publish-gate wedge >1h -- DETECTED: the wedge alert clears only on a successful publish (record_publish_gate_success) plus the eighth-class 2h age-cap on a blocked pending-batch. (3) Origin freeze >30m -- DETECTED (detector added after the incident): self-verifying push verifies ls-remote origin==HEAD; deadman keys on commits reaching origin. (4) Advisor restart-ruling -- NOT a machine detector by design: a policy reset condition (a staged doc doorbelling the machine awake resets the counter), enforced only by the unbuilt counter (Q2). Verdict: 2 of 4 have live detectors; the other 2 (console rescue, advisor-restart) are gated on building the exit-criterion counter. Primary state: background/deadmans_switch.py, d81197736 section 3.

a056615002f9.question: Staleness disposition in the gap taxonomy (27271871e section 3a).
a056615002f9.disposition: ANSWERED (2026-07-28 -- director-delegated 'your call', 27271871e section 3a): staleness is dispositioned as a READ-TIME FILTER in GAP1's reader contract, NOT a fifth bucket. Rationale: a stale row (superseded / already fixed / describes a removed component) is not a gap-category -- it is a data-quality condition on the row -- so a fifth bucket would break the four buckets' mutual-exclusion-over-LIVE-gaps and, under ambiguous-defaults-to-mint, manufacture work for a gap that no longer exists. The reader already verifies each row against primary state (LAW-C independent read); that is where staleness is detected. Evidence test: the row's primary-state referent no longer exists / is already closed -> the row is dropped before triage (not routed to a bucket). This is consistent with the fail-open fix already minted in PLANNER_MINTED_gap1_reader_contract_failopen_fix. Net: four buckets stay over live gaps; staleness is a pre-triage reader filter.

ded5e99d9b71.question: Blast radius as positive value versus risk (27271871e section 3b).
ded5e99d9b71.disposition: ANSWERED (2026-07-28 -- director-delegated, 27271871e section 3b): blast radius is DELIBERATELY FOLDED into value as a tie-breaker; risk is NOT scored separately. Honest basis (the ruling's own sanctioned disposition, 'if folded for simplicity, say so and leave it; not worth a mechanism'): for these gaps value and risk move together -- a gap touching many surfaces is both higher-value to fix and higher-risk to leave -- so a single blast-radius term serves both as the diagnostic tie-breaker. No separate risk axis exists in the ordering and none is warranted; left folded, no mechanism added. R12 respected: blast-radius is a tie-breaker diagnostic, never a target.
